machines.label: MPCNC
machines.tagline: Large-part router — side-plates, panels, structural frames. Also a portable demo machine used at outreach events.
machines.description: A DIY CNC router built from 3D-printed structural parts and common hardware, following the open-source MPCNC design. The team assembled and iterated it themselves. Because the entire robot is 100% CAD-designed, setting up toolpaths is straightforward — the machine cuts directly from Onshape exports. It's also portable and appears at outreach demos as a working example of student-built fabrication equipment.
machines.photoHint: MPCNC in the shop cutting a robot side-plate

machines.label: 6"×6" Mill
machines.tagline: Precision work — gears, tight-tolerance small parts
machines.description: A compact 6"×6" industrial mill reserved for high-tolerance detail work. Where the MPCNC handles bulk structural cuts, this machine handles the parts that demand tight tolerances — gear profiles, bearing pockets, and intricate mounting features. The precision ceiling here is meaningfully higher than what a printed-part router can deliver.
machines.photoHint: 6"×6" CNC mill cutting a gear profile

machines.label: PrintNC
machines.tagline: Large-scale cutting — full-sheet stock and oversized workpieces
machines.description: The largest CNC in the shop, a PrintNC build designed for cutting full-sheet stock. Its travel envelope handles workpieces that are too large for either the MPCNC or the 6"×6" mill. The team runs Production Hub jobs here — including parts machined for other FTC teams.
machines.photoHint: PrintNC running a full-sheet aluminum cut

machines.label: 3D Printing
machines.tagline: Rapid iteration — complex geometry, prototyping, jigs
machines.description: The team's primary FDM printer is the Bambu Lab X1C, paired with resin printers for detail work. FDM handles parts with geometry that would be difficult or slow to machine: curved channels, integrated snap features, cable routing guides, and sensor mounts. Prototypes are printed first to verify fit before committing a part to CNC time. The MPCNC itself is largely held together by printed components.
machines.photoHint: Bambu Lab X1C mid-run on a robot sensor mount

fabStat.context: Kit-based FTC robots use off-the-shelf structural components. GEarheads designs every structural and mechanical part from scratch in Onshape, then fabricates them on team-built CNC mills or with 3D printing. The Freight Frenzy season (2021–22) clocked in at ~90% custom-fabricated; every season since has been 100% custom — including three full robot iterations in DECODE (2025–26).

processSteps.label: CAD
processSteps.detail: Full robot modeled in Onshape with joints and motion simulation before any material is cut.

processSteps.label: CAM / Setup
processSteps.detail: Toolpaths generated from Onshape exports. Machine selected based on part size and tolerance requirements.

processSteps.label: Machining
processSteps.detail: MPCNC, 6"×6" mill, PrintNC, or the X1C runs the part. Manual finishing completes detail work.

processSteps.label: Finished Part
processSteps.detail: De-burred, tapped, and inspected. Assembled into the robot sub-system and tested immediately.

productionHub.description: The Production Hub runs CNC jobs for other FTC teams in Wisconsin who lack fabrication infrastructure. In the 2025–26 season, GEarheads completed 41 parts and provided fabrication coaching to four teams.
